Ah, that's a common Windows permission issue! It happens when a tool like shadcn or tailwind tries to scan folders (like Documents\My Pictures) that Windows protects.

✅ Here's How to Fix It:

✅ Option 1: Run VS Code as Administrator

  1. Close VS Code completely.

  2. Right-click the VS Code icon.

  3. Click “Run as administrator.”

  4. Open your project again and rerun:

bash
npx shadcn@latest init

This usually resolves the EPERM: operation not permitted error.

✅ Option 2: Create the Project in a Safer Directory

Instead of using Documents, try a directory like:

bash
C:\projects\assignment1

Steps:

bash
# Make a new folder outside Documents
mkdir C:\projects
cd C:\projects

# Create and enter your project folder
npx create-next-app@latest assignment1
cd assignment1

# Now run ShadCN safely
npx shadcn@latest init

'use client'

import { useState } from "react";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Card, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card";

const quotesData = [
  { topic: "success", quote: "Success is not final, failure is not fatal: It is the courage to continue that counts." },
  { topic: "success", quote: "Don't watch the clock; do what it does. Keep going." },
  { topic: "success", quote: "Success usually comes to those who are too busy to be looking for it." },
  { topic: "life", quote: "Life is what happens when you're busy making other plans." },
  { topic: "life", quote: "Get busy living or get busy dying." },
  { topic: "life", quote: "The purpose of our lives is to be happy." },
  { topic: "motivation", quote: "Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life." },
  { topic: "motivation", quote: "The harder you work for something, the greater you'll feel when you achieve it." },
  { topic: "motivation", quote: "Push yourself, because no one else is going to do it for you." }
];

export default function QuoteGenerator() {
  const [topic, setTopic] = useState("");
  const [quotes, setQuotes] = useState([]);

  const handleSubmit = (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const filtered = quotesData
      .filter(q => q.topic.toLowerCase() === topic.toLowerCase())
      .slice(0, 3);
    setQuotes(filtered);
  };

  return (
    <div className="max-w-xl mx-auto mt-10 p-4">
      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="flex gap-2 mb-6">
        <Input
          type="text"
          placeholder="Enter a topic (e.g. success, life, motivation)"
          value={topic}
          onChange={(e) => setTopic(e.target.value)}
        />
        <Button type="submit">Get Quotes</Button>
      </form>

      <div className="space-y-4">
        {quotes.length > 0 ? (
          quotes.map((q, idx) => (
            <Card key={idx}>
              <CardContent className="p-4 text-base font-medium">
                {q.quote}
              </CardContent>
            </Card>
          ))
        ) : (
          <p className="text-center text-muted-foreground">No quotes to display</p>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

🚀 Step 4: Run the App

In your terminal (inside assignment1), run:

bash
npm run dev

Then open http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

You’ll see your Quote Generator!
